fields.mechanism: Thermal heterogeneity and in-plane temperature gradients within the battery alter electrochemical behavior, causing localized resistance changes that mimic or trigger intermittent sensor fault codes during low thermal mass conditions.
fields.intervention: Implement a temperature-compensated voltage threshold algorithm for the battery monitoring unit that adjusts sensitivity based on real-time localized surface temperature readings rather than a static global threshold.
fields.expected_effect: The intermittent warning light flash at cold idle will cease because the system no longer misinterprets normal cold-temperature voltage drops/resistance increases as a critical charging fault.
fields.falsification_test: Perform a controlled cold-soak test below 0C with the engine idling; monitor the battery voltage hysteresis and log the thermal camera readings at the specific cell location; if the warning light remains off while static threshold triggers would have occurred, the intervention is confirmed.

fields.mechanism: Localized heat generation produces in-plane and through-thickness temperature gradients within lithium-ion cells, and these spatially non-uniform thermal distributions influence electrochemical behavior and safety, meaning that battery internal sensing must account for thermal heterogeneity rather than rely on a single-point measurement.
fields.intervention: Map the paper's multiscale, gradient-aware thermal sensing concept onto the 2015 Camry's charging system by instrumenting the 12V lead-acid battery (and its sensing/ground paths) with distributed temperature sensors (surface-mounted plus embedded/ring-terminal sensors) combined with a model-predictive diagnostic that interprets spatially distributed thermal data instead of a single battery current/temperature sensor; at cold idle (<0 C) the alternator's reduced output combined with high accessory load on a cold-weakened battery creates localized internal heating/resistance gradients that the OEM IBS misreads as a charging fault.
fields.expected_effect: The intermittent battery warning light flash at cold idle is resolved because the distributed thermal sensing detects the true localized electrochemical state of the battery rather than misinterpreting a cold-idle voltage/thermal transient as a charging-system fault, eliminating false battery warnings while preserving genuine fault detection.
fields.falsification_test: Connect a calibrated distributed thermal sensor array to a cold-soaked (<0 C) Camry battery, run the engine at idle until the warning light flashes, and capture the in-plane/through-thickness thermal gradient; if the gradient remains spatially uniform (ΔT < ~1 C across the cell) at the moment of the warning, the thermal-heterogeneity mechanism is falsified and the root cause must be elsewhere (e.g., IBS ground, alternator diode, or PCM logic).
fields.mechanism_source_span: Thermal heterogeneity accelerates capacity fade, drives localized degradation, and elevates the risk of thermal runaway (TR), particularly in high‐energy‐density and fast‐charging systems.

unique_mechanisms.claim: Thermal heterogeneity and in-plane temperature gradients within the battery alter electrochemical behavior, causing localized resistance changes that mimic or trigger intermittent sensor fault codes during low thermal mass conditions.
Temperature-dependent internal resistance and electrochemical behavior in cells

Localized heat generation produces in-plane and through-thickness temperature gradients within lithium-ion cells, and these spatially non-uniform thermal distributions influence electrochemical behavior and safety, meaning that battery internal sensing must account for thermal heterogeneity rather than rely on a single-point measurement.

Implement a temperature-compensated voltage threshold algorithm for the battery monitoring unit that adjusts sensitivity based on real-time localized surface temperature readings rather than a static global threshold.
Replace the voltage-sensing resistor or update the BMS temperature-compensation algorithm to account for increased internal resistance at sub-zero temperatures.

Map the paper's multiscale, gradient-aware thermal sensing concept onto the 2015 Camry's charging system by instrumenting the 12V lead-acid battery (and its sensing/ground paths) with distributed temperature sensors (surface-mounted plus embedded/ring-terminal sensors) combined with a model-predictive diagnostic that interprets spatially distributed thermal data instead of a single battery current/temperature sensor; at cold idle (<0 C) the alternator's reduced output combined with high accessory load on a cold-weakened battery creates localized internal heating/resistance gradients that the OEM IBS misreads as a charging fault.
The intermittent warning light flash at cold idle will cease because the system no longer misinterprets normal cold-temperature voltage drops/resistance increases as a critical charging fault.
Eliminates false low-voltage or high-current triggers that cause the intermittent warning light flash at cold idle.

The intermittent battery warning light flash at cold idle is resolved because the distributed thermal sensing detects the true localized electrochemical state of the battery rather than misinterpreting a cold-idle voltage/thermal transient as a charging-system fault, eliminating false battery warnings while preserving genuine fault detection.
